name: clone-finder
instructions:
Reach for find_clones INSTEAD of reading files to hunt for duplication yourself — the whole value of the tool is the context you did not spend reading.

The report is locations, not code: open only the places that look worth extracting.

A hit is a candidate, not a verdict. Duplication the detector finds is sometimes duplication worth keeping — three test fixtures that align are not always worth merging.

Do not lower min_tokens to be thorough. That is how the report becomes unusable: it floods with short repeated statements — six lines of assertions clears min_lines, and the token floor is what keeps them out.

tools.name: find_clones
tools.description: Finds duplicated code and reports where it is, without you reading the files. Returns ranked locations and a few lines of each block, biggest duplication first.

path.description: Directory to scan, e.g. . or src/ — searched recursively.

min_lines.description: Shortest block to report. Default 6. Both floors must be cleared.

min_tokens.description: Fewest tokens to report. Default 50. Lowering this floods the report with short repeated statements — six lines of assertions clears min_lines but not this.

exclude.description: Glob of paths to skip, on top of build output and .gitignore, e.g. **/tests/**

max_results.description: How many findings to return, biggest first. Default 20; the report always says how many it omitted.
